title: Home & everyday objects
goal: Describe your home, say where things are (in, on, under, next to) and say 'there is / there isn't' and 'I have'.
intro:
A traditional Sindhi house is built around an **اڱڻ** (aṅaṇu, courtyard), where the family sits, sleeps on charpais in summer and receives visitors. City flats in Karachi and Hyderabad are different, but the words are the same.

This unit teaches the **postpositions of place** — Sindhi's equivalents of 'in, on, under', which come *after* the noun — and how to say 'there is', 'there isn't' (the very common **ڪونهي**) and 'I have' (**مون وٽ … آهي**).

vocab.note: m · pl ڪمرا kamirā; oblique ڪمري kamire (ڪمري ۾ = in the room).
f. Shah Latif's town is ڀٽ Bhiṭ — a different word ('sand dune').
f. People sleep on the roof on hot nights.
m. Toilet: ٽوائليٽ or پاخانو (more direct).
f. بتي هلي وئي = the power went off (load-shedding).
m. An ordinary (smaller) plate is ٿالهي thālhī (f); also پليٽ pleṭa (f).
Written with the special Sindhi sign ۾.
ٽيبل تي = on the table; ڪم تي = at work.
مون وٽ = with me / I have; ڊاڪٽر وٽ = at the doctor's.
Very common in speech instead of ناهي. Plural ڪونهن konhin.

phrases.native: منهنجو گهر ٻئي ماڙ تي آهي.
phrases.roman: munhinjo gharu ɓie māṛa te āhe.
phrases.en: My flat is on the second floor.
There's no water in the kitchen.

grammar.title: Postpositions of place: ۾، تي، هيٺ، ڀرسان …
grammar.body:
Sindhi uses **postpositions** — they come **after** the noun: ڪمري ۾ 'room in' = in the room. The noun before a postposition takes its **oblique** form:

masculine -o → -e: ڪمرو → **ڪمري ۾** kamire meṃ 'in the room'
masculine -u → -a: گهر → **گهر ۾** ghara meṃ 'in the house'
feminine -ī → -īa (written ءَ): الماري → **الماريءَ ۾** almārīa meṃ
other feminines usually don't change: کٽ → کٽ تي

The main place words: **۾** meṃ (in), **تي** te (on, at), **هيٺ** heṭhi (under), **مٿان** mathāṃ (on top of), **ڀرسان** bharsāṃ (next to), **اڳيان** aɠiyāṃ (in front of), **پويان** poyāṃ (behind), **وٽ** vaṭi (near, at someone's). With pronouns use the oblique: مون وٽ, هن ڀرسان.

examples.en: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the bed.
The clothes are in the cupboard.
The shop is next to the mosque.
examples.note: ڀرسان can also take جي before it.

examples.en: The car is in front of the house.

grammar.title: 'There is', 'there isn't' and 'I have'
grammar.body:
**There is / are** is just آهي / آهن, usually with the place first: ڪمري ۾ ٻه کٽون آهن 'In the room there are two beds'.

**There isn't** is ناهي (nāhe) or, very commonly in speech, **ڪونهي** (konhe; plural ڪونهن): رڌڻي ۾ کنڊ ڪونهي 'There's no sugar in the kitchen'.

**To have** (things) Sindhi says 'with me is': **مون وٽ** … آهي. For relatives, body parts and things that are part of you, use the possessive or کي instead: منهنجا ٻه ڀائر آهن, هن کي ٻه ٻار آهن.

examples.en: There are two beds in the room.
There's no sugar in the kitchen.

dialogue.title: Where are my keys?
dialogue.setting: Bilawal is late for work and can't find his keys. His mother helps.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: پوءِ کٽ هيٺ ڏس، يا الماريءَ ۾.
lines.roman: poi khaṭa heṭhi ɗisu, yā almārīa meṃ.
lines.en: Then look under the bed, or in the cupboard.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: هتي به ڪونهي! اوهه، دير ٿي وئي.
lines.roman: hite bi konhe! oh, dera thī vaī.
lines.en: Not here either! Oh, I'm late.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.roman: radhaṇe meṃ āhe, frija jī mathāṃ.
lines.en: It's in the kitchen, on top of the fridge.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.roman: ai mānī? moṃ vaṭi tayāru āhe.
lines.en: And food? I have it ready.

culture: Many Sindhi village homes have an **اوطاق** (autāqu) — a men's guest room or sitting place, often separate from the family quarters, where visitors are received, news is exchanged and music and poetry are shared late into the night. In summer, when temperatures in Sindh can pass 45°C, families sleep outdoors in the courtyard or on the roof on charpais. Shoes are usually taken off before entering a room with carpets or floor seating.

tip.title: In, on: ۾ and تي come after
tip.body:
- Sindhi says 'room in', 'table on': ڪمري **۾**, ٽيبل **تي**.
- Before them, -o nouns change to -e: ڪمرو → **ڪمري ۾**, رڌڻو → رڌڻي ۾.
- -u nouns change only in sound: گهر gharu → ghara ۾.

lessons.title: Under the bed, behind the door

tip.title: Under, on top, next to
tip.body:
- These come after the noun too: کٽ **هيٺ** under the bed, الماريءَ **مٿان** on top of the cupboard.
- **ڀرسان** next to, **اڳيان** in front of, **پويان** behind usually take **جي** first: در **جي** پويان.
- Feminine -ī nouns add ءَ: الماري → الماريءَ ۾, دري → دريءَ جي ڀرسان.

The key is on top of the cupboard.
The chair is next to the table.

lessons.title: There's no water! I don't have it

tip.title: There is, there isn't, I have
tip.body:
- 'There is' is just **آهي** (plural **آهن**): ڪمري ۾ ٽي ڪرسيون آهن.
- 'There isn't' in everyday speech: **ڪونهي** (plural **ڪونهن**).
- 'I have (a thing)' = 'with me is': **مون وٽ** … آهي. Also توهان وٽ, هن وٽ, اسان وٽ.

new: منهنجو گهر ٻئي ماڙ تي آهي.
